## scene.info

Name, asset, modification and play state, entity count and settings of the edited scene, and what runs while playing (running: the running scene, which a game's scene switch makes another than the edited one; null in edit mode; see play.state). entityCount counts the active scene's entities (the running one while playing); settings.physicsLayers are the project's collision layers as the active scene runs them. settings.fixedRate is the step the active scene runs: source project when the project's Scene.Timing FixedRate sets it (project.setSettings), scene for its own fixedTimestep.

## scene.loadAdditive

Loads a scene asset into the running game next to what it holds (a sub-scene, as scripts' Scene:\:LoadAdditive does; play mode only: play.stop ends it with the game). The scene and everything it uses load in the background, then its entities are created over the following frames (at most the scene's maxEntitiesInstantiatedPerFrame per frame), keeping their IDs: a sub-scene whose IDs the running scene has already (the same scene twice) fails. Answers once every entity exists: {subScene (its number, for scene.unloadAdditive), scene, state, progress, createdEntities, skippedEntities, totalEntities, slices, roots (the top-level entities), seconds, frames}. scene.loadStatus reports sub-scenes while they load.

Kind: `Edit` · Results: `Content` · MCP toolsets: `scene` · Answers later (MayDefer): yes · Waits for the asset scan: yes · Registered at `StrataEditor/src/Editor/EditorSceneCommands.cpp:458`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `scene` | string | yes |   | Scene asset to load into the running scene (asset handle, or path relative to the asset directory). |

## scene.loadStatus

The scene loads under way: open (the scene scene.open, or project.open for the project's start scene, is opening: {scene, startScene, state: LoadingScene \| LoadingDependencies \| Preparing (its render proxies are built for the viewport), progress 0 to 1}, null when none), lastOpen (the latest of those that finished: {scene, startScene, state: Ready \| Failed \| Cancelled, error, seconds}, null before the first), play (the scene a running game asked for while it loads, {scene, progress}, null when none) and subScenes (the running scene's sub-scenes, scene.loadAdditive: {subScene, scene, state: Loading \| Instantiating \| Loaded \| Failed, progress, createdEntities, skippedEntities (not created because an ancestor was deleted while the sub-scene loaded), totalEntities, slices, error}) and world (the cells the open world streams around the editor camera, editor, and while playing those of the running game, game: each {cellsWanted, cellsLoading, cellsLoaded, cellsUnloading, cellsPinned, cellsFailed} or null; null when no world streams). With wait, it answers once no scene is being opened, e.g. after starting an editor with a window, which opens its project's start scene in the background (scene edits and play.start fail until then).

## scene.new

Replaces the edited scene with a new, unsaved one: empty by default, or with a template's content, e.g. &quot;basic3d&quot; (a lit start: camera, sun, procedural sky, ground, post-processing; the editor camera then looks through the scene's camera; the ground's material Materials/Ground.stmat is added to a project that lacks it). Fails while the edited scene has unsaved changes unless force is true (save first). Save the new scene with scene.saveAs. Waits for saves in flight (scene.save) first. Returns discardedChanges (whether unsaved changes were discarded).

Kind: `Edit` · Results: `Content` · MCP toolsets: `scene` · Answers later (MayDefer): yes · Waits for the asset scan: yes · Registered at `StrataEditor/src/Editor/EditorSceneCommands.cpp:379`

| `force` | boolean | no |   | Go on although the edited scene has unsaved changes, discarding them (default false: the command fails instead). Discarded changes are kept as recovery data of the project (scene.recoveryStatus), and the person at the editor is told who discarded them. |
| `name` | string | no |   | Scene name. |
| `template` | string | no |   | What the scene starts with (default &quot;empty&quot;; see project.templates). One of: `empty`, `basic3d`. |

## scene.open

Opens a scene asset for editing. Fails while the edited scene has unsaved changes unless force is true (save first); waits for saves in flight (scene.save) before it decides. The scene is read and loaded with everything it uses in the background while the editor goes on showing the edited scene, which stays read-only meanwhile (edits and play.start fail); the command answers once the opened scene replaced it: {scene, name, entities, discardedChanges (whether unsaved changes were discarded), seconds, frames, frameTimes (the CPU time of the frames that ran meanwhile: count, medianMs, meanMs, p95Ms, maxMs)}. Opening another scene, scene.new or closing the project cancels it. scene.loadStatus (and editor.status's sceneLoad) report its progress.

## scene.raycast

What a ray, or a pixel of the Scene view, hits among what the active scene draws: its mesh renderers, on their triangles (their bounds while a mesh loads). Give origin and direction, or viewport {x, y, width?, height?} (a pixel of the Scene view's image, through its camera: the editor camera, or the scene's primary camera with Game camera on). maxDistance limits the ray (default: unlimited for origin and direction, the view's far plane for a pixel); ignore leaves entities out with their descendants. Returns {hit: true, entity, name, point, normal (facing the ray's origin), distance, onTriangle (false: a loading mesh's bounds were hit), ray: {origin, direction}} or {hit: false, ray}; ray is what asset.place {ray} takes. Colliders, gizmos and UI are not hit. While playing it casts into the running game.

Kind: `Query` · Results: `Content` · MCP toolsets: `scene` · Answers later (MayDefer): no · Waits for the asset scan: no · Registered at `StrataEditor/src/Editor/Commands/PlacementCommands.cpp:392`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `direction` | array of number | no |   | Where the ray points, any length but zero (with origin). Items: at least 3, at most 3. |
| `ignore` | array of string | no |   | Entities left out, with their descendants (entity IDs). Items: at least 1. |
| `maxDistance` | number | no |   | How far along the ray to look, in meters (default: unlimited for a ray, the view's far plane for a pixel). Value: more than `0`. |
| `origin` | array of number | no |   | Where the ray starts, in world space (with direction). Items: at least 3, at most 3. |
| `viewport` | object | no |   | A pixel of the Scene view's image, cast through its camera (instead of origin and direction). |
| `viewport.height` | integer | no |   | The height of that image (default: the Scene view's, or 720). Value: at least `1`, at most `16384`. |
| `viewport.width` | integer | no |   | The width of the image the pixel refers to (default: the Scene view's, or 1280 while it has none). Value: at least `1`, at most `16384`. |
| `viewport.x` | number | yes |   | Pixels from the image's left edge, continuous: the middle of the first column is 0.5. |
| `viewport.y` | number | yes |   | Pixels from the image's top edge, continuous. |

## scene.recover

Applies or discards recovery data (scene.recoveryStatus). apply: opens the scene the changes were made to in the background as scene.open does (a scene never saved: a new scene of its name) and, once it is in, turns it into what the edits left, as one undo step back to the saved scene (a world's changes wait until the cells they name are loaded, and go back into them); the scene stays modified (save it to keep the changes). It refuses when the scene file changed since the changes were made (applicable false), while playing, while a scene is being opened (scene.loadStatus), and while the edited scene has unsaved changes it would discard unless force is true; it waits for saves in flight (scene.save) first. discard: moves the data to .strata/Recovery/Discarded, where it is not offered again. Returns {recovered \| discarded: id, ...}; apply also scene, sceneName, entities (how many it restored or removed) and discardedChanges.

Kind: `Session` · Results: `Content` · MCP toolsets: `scene` · Answers later (MayDefer): yes · Waits for the asset scan: yes · Registered at `StrataEditor/src/Editor/EditorStateCommands.cpp:604`

| `force` | boolean | no |   | Go on although the edited scene has unsaved changes, discarding them (default false: the command fails instead). Discarded changes are kept as recovery data of the project (scene.recoveryStatus), and the person at the editor is told who discarded them. |
| `scene` | string | yes |   | The id of an entry of scene.recoveryStatus, or a scene asset (handle or path) to use its newest applicable entry. |

## scene.recoveryStatus

The recovery data of the open project (.strata/Recovery): unsaved scene changes an editor left behind when it ended without closing the scene (a crash), or that were discarded on purpose (force, Don't Save) and kept anyway. Returns entries, newest first, each {id, scene (null for a scene never saved), sceneName, scenePath, time (milliseconds since 1970-01-01 UTC), discarded, entityCount, complete (a snapshot of every entity), applicable, problem (why it cannot be applied, e.g. the scene was saved since)}, and the journal of the edited scene {active, file, writes, lastWrite, pending (changes not written yet: they are written about 2 s after edits stop), pendingSteps (undo steps waiting for that write), busy, skipped (why its changes are not journaled)}. Reads the directory again, after the journal writes already asked for; while the project's assets are scanned it answers once they are (entries are judged against them). Apply or discard an entry with scene.recover. Fails without a project.

Kind: `Query` · Results: `Session` · MCP toolsets: `scene` · Answers later (MayDefer): yes · Waits for the asset scan: yes · Registered at `StrataEditor/src/Editor/EditorStateCommands.cpp:574`

No parameters.

```json
  "properties": {},
  "type": "object"
}
```

## scene.save

Saves the edited scene to its asset in the background and answers once the file is written (wait false: at once). The frame only takes a snapshot of the scene, the document is written on a background thread, and edits made meanwhile stay unsaved (the save holds the scene as it was when the command ran). With wait (default true) the answer comes once the file is written and published: {scene, path, bytes, entities, seconds, frames, frameTimes (the editor's frames meanwhile: count, medianMs, meanMs, p95Ms, maxMs), memory {privateMBBefore, peakPrivateMBDuring}}. With wait false it answers at once with {scene, path, saveId, state: Writing \| Queued}; editor.status's saving lists the saves in flight. A save queues behind one that writes. New scenes need scene.saveAs first. A world's persistent scene saves the documents changed since the last save, in the background too: the persistent scene (without the cells' entities), each dirty cell and then the world's document with those cells' index entries; documents lists them ({path, kind: persistent, cell or world, bytes, entities}; bytes and entities are their sums), and a world's save waits for its previous one.

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `wait` | boolean | no |   | Answer once the document is written (default true); false answers at once with the save's saveId. |

## scene.saveAs

Saves the edited scene as a new .stscene asset and continues editing it: the scene takes the file's name and the new asset at once (a following scene.save writes it), and gets the previous ones back when the save fails. The save runs in the background like scene.save's and answers like it (wait, default true: once written; false: at once with its saveId).

## scene.setSettings

Changes settings of the edited scene: gravity, the fixed step, the physics world's capacities, and how many entities additive loads (sub-scenes) create per frame (undoable, one step). Capacities take effect when a physics world is created, at the next play start, so set them in edit mode. While playing, changes go to the running copy only and play.stop discards them (the result then has a warning). Collision layers are the project's: set them with project.setCollisionLayers. The project's fixed rate (Scene.Timing, project.setSettings) overrides fixedTimestep and maxFixedStepsPerFrame; they apply when its FixedRate is Scene (a change is stored either way, with a warning). Returns the settings with the step the scene runs (fixedRate) and the collision layers it runs with (scene.info shows them too).

Kind: `Edit` · Results: `Content` · MCP toolsets: `scene` · Answers later (MayDefer): no · Waits for the asset scan: yes · Registered at `StrataEditor/src/Editor/EditorSceneCommands.cpp:569`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `fixedTimestep` | number | no |   | Fixed simulation step in seconds (1/1000 to 1/10). |
| `gravity` | array of number | no |   | Gravity in m/s^2. Items: at least 3, at most 3. |
| `layerCollisions` | any | no |   | Refused since 0.6.0: collision layers are the project's, set with project.setCollisionLayers (same parameter). Deprecated. |
| `layerNames` | any | no |   | Refused since 0.6.0: collision layers are the project's, set with project.setCollisionLayers (same parameter). Deprecated. |
| `maxEntitiesDestroyedPerFrame` | integer | no |   | Entities sub-scenes being unloaded (scene.unloadAdditive, scripts' SubScene:\:Unload, a world's cells) may destroy per frame, all together (default 5000); creation and destruction together stop after about 2 ms a frame. Value: at least `1`, at most `1048576`. |
| `maxEntitiesInstantiatedPerFrame` | integer | no |   | Entities sub-scenes loading into the scene (scene.loadAdditive, scripts' Scene:\:LoadAdditive) may create per frame, all together (default 5000); each frame also stops creating after about 2 ms. Value: at least `1`, at most `1048576`. |
| `maxFixedStepsPerFrame` | integer | no |   | Upper bound of fixed steps per frame. Value: at least `1`, at most `64`. |
| `physicsCapacity` | object | no |   | Physics world room (only the given values change), reserved when play starts (up to 131072 bodies and 262144 contacts at once; beyond that it counts for growth only); raise it for scenes that create many bodies while they play, so that the world does not grow during play. |
| `physicsCapacity.maxBodies` | integer | no |   | Bodies the physics world has room for when play starts (each about 2 KiB); 0 sizes it from the bodies the scene starts with. The world grows beyond it while bodies are created. Value: at least `0`, at most `2097152`. |
| `physicsCapacity.maxBodyPairs` | any | no |   | Ignored since 0.5.0 (box3d has no buffer of body pairs to size); accepted for older command scripts, with a warning. Deprecated. |
| `physicsCapacity.maxContactConstraints` | integer | no |   | Contacts the physics world has room for when play starts (each about 250 bytes); 0: automatic. Value: at least `0`, at most `524288`. |
| `resetLayerCollisions` | any | no |   | Refused since 0.6.0: collision layers are the project's, set with project.setCollisionLayers (same parameter). Deprecated. |

## scene.unloadAdditive

Removes a sub-scene from the running game (play mode only): stops its load, releasing what it held loaded, and takes its entities out of the game at once (inactive: no rendering, scripts' updates, physics or audio); they are destroyed with their descendants over the following frames (at most the scene's maxEntitiesDestroyedPerFrame a frame; their scripts get OnDestroy; scene.loadStatus shows the sub-scene Unloading with destroyedEntities until its last entity is gone). Returns {subScene, entities (the running scene's count now), unloadingEntities (those still to destroy)}.

Kind: `Edit` · Results: `Content` · MCP toolsets: `scene` · Answers later (MayDefer): no · Waits for the asset scan: yes · Registered at `StrataEditor/src/Editor/EditorSceneCommands.cpp:477`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `subScene` | integer | yes |   | The sub-scene's number (scene.loadAdditive, scene.loadStatus). Value: at least `1`, at most `9223372036854775807`. |
